questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the neocerebellum?

options.text: Planning and programming of voluntary movements

questions.correctAnswerText: Planning and programming of voluntary movements
questions.explanation:
The function of the neocerebellum is planning and programming of voluntary movements.
The cerebellum can be divided into:
The Vestibulocerebellum/Archicerebellum: Consists principally of the flocculonodular lobe and adjacent portions of the vermis. It participates in balance, vestibular reflexes, and eye movements.
The Spinocerebellum/Paleocerebellum: Consists of most of the vermis plus the adjacent intermediate zones on both sides of the vermis. It coordinates movements of the limbs. Vermis: Proximal muscles, Intermediate zones: Distal muscles.
The Cerebrocerebellum/neocerebellum: Consists of the large lateral zones of the cerebellar hemispheres. It receives all its input from the cerebral cortex (motor, premotor and somatosensory). It transmits its output back to the brain, functioning in a feedback manner to plan sequential voluntary body and limb movements.
questions.structuredExplanationText:
The function of the neocerebellum is planning and programming of voluntary movements.
The cerebellum can be divided into:
The Vestibulocerebellum/Archicerebellum: Consists principally of the flocculonodular lobe and adjacent portions of the vermis. It participates in balance, vestibular reflexes, and eye movements.
The Spinocerebellum/Paleocerebellum: Consists of most of the vermis plus the adjacent intermediate zones on both sides of the vermis. It coordinates movements of the limbs. Vermis: Proximal muscles, Intermediate zones: Distal muscles.
The Cerebrocerebellum/neocerebellum: Consists of the large lateral zones of the cerebellar hemispheres. It receives all its input from the cerebral cortex (motor, premotor and somatosensory). It transmits its output back to the brain, functioning in a feedback manner to plan sequential voluntary body and limb movements.

+ Decomposition of movement - Lack of smooth flow of movement.

« Speech defect - Staccato speech or slurring speech

+ Pendular knee jerk (a feature of hypotonia)

+ Intention tremors.

« Nystagmus (jerky movements of the eye)

«Rebound phenomenon

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Inhibition of Purkinje cells by stellate cells is an example of _____.

options.text: Stellate cells doesn’t inhibit Purkinje cells

questions.explanation:
Inhibition of Purkinje cells by stellate cells is an example of feedforward inhibition.

Mossy fibers exert a weak excitatory effect on many Purkinje cells via the granule cells. The
granule cells also excite the basket and stellate cells via their parallel fibers. The basket and
stellate cells, in turn, inhibit the Purkinje cells (Feed forward inhibition)

Renshaw cells exhibit feed back inhibition.

granule cells also excite the basket and stellate cells via their parallel fibers. The basket and
stellate cells, in turn, inhibit the Purkinje cells (Feed forward inhibition)

Renshaw cells exhibit feed back inhibition.
